name: Gemini CLI
note: Gemini CLI keeps no durable session record: ~/.gemini holds settings, a project list and a .project_root marker per directory, and nothing that describes a conversation. There is no transcript to read, so there are no tokens, no cost and no context figure — and a row that showed zeros would be claiming knowledge this harness does not have. It contributes presence only: the running process, the directory it is working in, and an explicit note that the rest is unknown. The process rule matches the executable name exactly: a path fragment of /bin/gemini also matches /bin/geminid, which the negative probe caught — the second time that check has found an over-broad matcher of mine. Context files are GEMINI.md: the CLI's documentation names ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md as the global one and GEMINI.md in the workspace as the project one. Only the workspace file itself is probed — the CLI also walks parent directories and, just in time, the directories a tool touches, which is not something a probe at the session's working directory can see. Skills live in .agents/skills or .gemini/skills, with the .agents alias taking precedence, and in the same two folders under home. The default context file name can be changed in settings; a renamed one reads as absent rather than wrong.
